subject: Nonlinear tier path and feature carveout discussion
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@claresys.com>
Cc: Tom Elias <tom.elias@claresys.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Nonlinear tier path and feature carveout discussion

Hi Maya / Tom,

Thanks again for the time last week — helpful to see how your gen-AI assistant pilot is shaping up. I pulled together a short mapping of how ClareSys's usage profile might map to our tiers and where a carveout for the fine-tuning / private model capability would make sense.

High level:
- Core throughput & embeddings needs fit our Compact tier for the pilot.
- Two features (private fine-tuning + long-context KV caching) push toward a Custom/Hybrid pack unless we carve them out as add-ons.

I've attached a proposal (bundle-proposal-v2.pdf) with three options: a) stay Compact + paid add-ons for fine-tune & KV cache, b) Hybrid pack that includes both at a blended commit, c) Dedicated Reserved pool for the fine-tune workload and Compact for general inference.

Key questions for you:
1) Would ClareSys prefer a single blended package or a Compact baseline with explicit add-ons?
2) Do you need an SLA on the fine-tune job runtime, or is throughput within a weekly window acceptable?

If helpful, we can run a short workshop (30–45m) this week to make the decision and record the mutual action plan. Proposed time windows attached in the doc.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: claresys-bundle-proposal-v2.pdf
From: Maya Singh <maya@claresys.com>

Cc: Tom Elias <tom.elias@claresys.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonlinear tier path and feature carveout discussion

Thanks Sergio — this is exactly what we needed to see. A couple quick clarifications from my side:

- For the pilot (Q1), we want predictable spend and the ability to turn the fine-tune capability on/off per team. If the add-on approach nets a lower committed monthly than Hybrid, that's prefered.
- We will likely need a 99.5% availability target for the inference endpoint (not the fine-tune batch jobs). Can you confirm which options include that?

Also looping in Tom since he will own procurement/contracting on our side. Tom — can you share any constraints on annual vs monthly commits?

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Product, ClareSys
maya@claresys.com

Sergio —

Procurement constraints: ClareSys prefers annual commitments for core services. We can do a shorter-month commitment for experimental add-ons but would need visibility into unit pricing and expected overage billing. If Hybrid reduces operational friction, procurement may accept a blended annual commit but we'll need a clear stepdown plan.

I'll aim to be available for a workshop on Thursday afternoon.

—Tom
VP Finance Ops, ClareSys
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@claresys.com>, Tom Elias <tom.elias@claresys.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonlinear tier path and feature carveout discussion

Looping in product & pricing to clarify options for the workshop. Sergio / Ben — quick summary margin/discount constraints to prep: 

- If ClareSys wants annual blended commit (Hybrid option), we can offer up to a 22% enterprise discount on list for a 12-month commit at the RDW-7682 estimated ARR band, provided we keep the fine-tune compute on a shared Dedicated pool rather than a per-customer reserved host.
- Add-on approach (Compact + add-ons) keeps base price list but we can provide a volume-based tiered discount on add-ons (10% at $5k+/month, 18% at $20k+/month).
- We should prepare an explicit stepdown path in the MAP: what features remain if they drop from Hybrid to Compact mid-year (KV cache disabled, fine-tune becomes metered batch).

Maya / Tom — I recommend the workshop include: decision owner (Maya), procurement (Tom), engineering constraints (one of your engineers), and Redwood pricing owner (Ben).

If those attendees look right I can draft a one-page MAP and share before the call.

—Lauren
VP, Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: claresys-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nonlinear tier path and feature carveout discussion

Thanks all — great alignment in the workshop earlier today. Quick recap and next steps (action items for MAP):

1) Decision: ClareSys will sign a 12-month Hybrid commit that includes Compact baseline + bundled fine-tune add-on (Hybrid option B). Procurement approved annual commit contingent on a documented stepdown.
2) Discount / economics: Redwood to provide 20% enterprise discount on the blended commit (finalized in redlined SOW). Pricing owner: Ben Carter.
3) SLA & ops: 99.5% inference SLA included; fine-tune jobs will be run on shared Dedicated pool with agreed weekly maintenance windows.
4) Stepdown path: If ClareSys reduces to Compact-only mid-term, they retain embeddings and standard throughput; fine-tune becomes metered (per-job pricing) and KV cache becomes an optional paid add-on.
5) Deliverables: Redwood will circulate a draft SOW (with discount language) and the MAP by EOD Monday. Documents: claresys-bundle-proposal-v2.pdf, claresys-mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

Next meeting: contract redlines touchpoint scheduled for 2026-12-10 10:00 AM PT.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
